Major_Ice_Shelves_Present: George VI Ice Shelf (sound), Wilkins Ice Shelf, Bach Ice Shelf, Stange Ice Shelf
Physical_Mechanism: George VI is confined in a narrow (25 km) sound between Palmer Land and Alexander Island; high lateral shear stress.
Vulnerability_to_Collapse: Low structural collapse risk due to compressive geometry, but HIGH basal melt from Bellingshausen CDW.
Historical_Calibration_Data: MEaSUREs/ITS_LIVE velocities (1996–2024); BedMachine V4.1 sound bathymetry; Lucchitta & Rosanova (1998).
Identifiability_Status: Moderate (Degenerate with basal friction in steady state; identifiable via sub-shelf thinning rates).

Major_Ice_Shelves_Present: Small, disconnected marine-terminating tidewater glaciers; localized fringing ice shelves
Physical_Mechanism: Steep bedrock drops directly into deep fjords; minimal floating shelf area; discharge governed by calving front geometry.
Vulnerability_to_Collapse: Not vulnerable to shelf collapse (shelves already mostly absent); sensitive to frontal calving and ocean melt.
Historical_Calibration_Data: Cook et al. (2016) frontal retreat database; ASTER/Landsat calving margins; ITS_LIVE velocity fields.
Identifiability_Status: High (Discharge is primarily geometric; buttressing variations are second-order).

Major_Ice_Shelves_Present: Larsen A (collapsed 1995), Larsen B (collapsed 2002), Larsen C (intact, outer margin calved A68 in 2017)
Buttressing_Parameter_Range: theta_buttress in [0.00, 0.85] (Pre-2002: ~0.80; Post-2002: 0.00 for Crane/Flask/Jorum; Larsen C: ~0.75)
Physical_Mechanism: Larsen B provided critical back-stress. Its collapse removed lateral resistive margins, triggering 2x–8x acceleration.
Vulnerability_to_Collapse: EXTREME: Larsen C is vulnerable to hydrofracture if surface melt increases by 1.5–2.0°C (Trusel et al. 2015).
Historical_Calibration_Data: ERS-1/2, Envisat InSAR, ITS_LIVE velocities (1995–2024); Scambos et al. (2004); Rignot et al. (2004); Rott et al. (2018).
Identifiability_Status: EXCELLENT (2002 collapse provides an ideal natural experiment uniquely identifying the buttressing response).
